title: Carrying and disposing of full waste bags
audience: Cleaners who move full waste bags from the bin to the outside collection point on a route.
learningOutcomes: Keep a waste bag to a weight that can be lifted and carried safely by one person.
Remove a full bag from a bin using a method that protects the back and the hands.
Dispose of a bag at an outside bin by placing it by hand, never by throwing it.

instruction.heading: Keep the load manageable
instruction.body: A full bag is often the heaviest thing a cleaner lifts on a route. Keep each bag to a weight you can carry comfortably, with a clear view ahead. If a bag is very heavy, split it into two smaller bags or use the bin's wheels rather than heaving it. Do not overfill a bin, because a heavy bag is harder to pull out and more likely to split.

instruction.heading: Removing a bag from a bin
instruction.body: Tie the bag closed before you move it. Tip the bin onto its side and draw the bag out, keeping your back straight and bending at the knees. If the bag sticks because a vacuum has formed inside the bin, stop and ask the site contact whether small air holes can be added to that bin. Do not alter a bin yourself, because it may belong to the building.

instruction.heading: Getting bags into the outside bin
instruction.body: Never throw a bag from a distance. Walk up to the outside bin, lift the lid, and place the bag inside by hand. Do not lean into the bin or stand on its edge. Never press waste down with a hand or a foot. If the bin needs compacting, use a tool made for the job rather than a body part, because sharp items can be hidden in the waste.

procedure: Tie the bag closed before moving it.
Check the weight; split the bag if it is too heavy to carry comfortably.
Tip the bin, draw the bag out, and keep the back straight to lift.
Carry the bag to the outside bin, walking, with a clear view ahead.
Lift the lid, place the bag inside by hand, and close the lid.
Return the empty bin to its place on the route.

workedExamples.situation: A bag is hard to lift, and the bin seems to pull at the bag as it comes out.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop and do not yank the bag. Check its weight, and if it is too heavy split it into two smaller bags. If a vacuum holds the bag inside the bin, ask the site contact whether air holes can be added to that bin, and do not alter it yourself. Record the issue on the site card.

equipmentAndPpe: Sack trolley, where the site provides one

commonErrors.error: Lifting a bag from the waist with a twisted back.
commonErrors.prevention: Squat with a straight back and keep the bag close to the body.

commonErrors.error: Overfilling bins, so the bag becomes hard to lift out.
commonErrors.prevention: Empty the bin before it reaches the top, and split heavy bags.

commonErrors.error: Throwing bags into an outside bin.
commonErrors.prevention: Walk to the bin and place the bag by hand.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Manual handling is a common source of injury. The methods here are general practice.
Check an outside bin for sharp items and hazards before reaching in. Do not reach in blind.

qualityStandard: Each bag is tied and within a weight that can be carried safely by one person.
No bag is thrown into an outside bin.
Bins are returned empty to their places.
documentationEvidence: Strains, near misses or bin faults reported to the site contact on the same day.
summary: Keep bags to a carryable weight, and split them when they are too heavy.
Squat with a straight back, tip the bin, and draw the bag out without twisting.
Place bags in outside bins by hand; never throw or press waste down by hand or foot.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the safest way to get a full bag out of a bin?
options: Tie it closed, tip the bin, and draw the bag out while bending at the knees
Pull it out by the top while twisting at the waist and let it drop
Lift the whole bin onto your shoulder and shake the bag out and let it fall

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a bag be placed into an outside bin?
options: Walked up to and placed by hand

knowledgeChecks.question: Can hands or feet be used to press waste down inside a bin?
options: Yes, if the waste is light and loose
No, because hidden sharp items may be inside
Yes, provided gloves are always worn
